title: Any finite type closed subscheme of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme sits in an almost blowup square
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated X and a closed subscheme Z cut out by a finite type quasi-coherent ideal, the lemma asserts the existence of an almost blow up square as in equation labelled equation-almost-blow-up-square (statement lines 11086-11092). The proof writes X as a directed limit of Noetherian schemes with affine transition morphisms by Limits, Proposition labelled limits-proposition-approximate, descends the closed immersion Z -> X to some index by Limits, Lemmas labelled limits-lemma-descend-finite-presentation and limits-lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, and takes b_i : X'_i -> X_i the blowing up with center Z_i (proof lines 11094-11104). The resulting blow up square has all morphisms finite type between Noetherian schemes, hence of finite presentation, so it is an almost blow up square, and Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-almost-blow-up shows that its base change to X is the desired one (proof lines 11106-11115). Descending the subscheme and recognising the Noetherian blowup square as almost blowup, then transporting it by base change, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
